public_rationale: Studies from late 2024 report continued failures in all four areas on new or varied problems. Apple's GSM-Symbolic study found that adding one irrelevant clause cut math accuracy by up to 65% across state-of-the-art models. A causal reasoning study found LLMs rely on shallow cues such as event order. An embodied physics study found children outperform LLMs. A theory-of-mind robustness study found only limited ability. There is real counterevidence. OpenAI's o1 reached 74-83% on AIME 2024. A Nature Human Behaviour paper found GPT-4 at human level on several theory-of-mind tests, though it still struggled with faux pas. These gains are real, but they do not show that the trouble is gone. On the plain reading, 'still has trouble' fits the record at the time of the post.
limitations: 'Trouble' is qualitative; strong gains in some benchmarks (o1 math, GPT-4 theory of mind) mean the trouble is uneven.
Some supporting studies did not test the newest reasoning models.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs still have trouble with causality, physical, psychological and mathematical reasoning, even if they now pass the specific published examples.
conditions: even if they now solve the specific published examples

statement.excerpt: Ernest Davis and I wrote in 2020 in Technology Review that GPT-3 was “a fluent spouter of bullshit” that had trouble with causality, physical reasoning, psychological reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and so on. All that’s still true, even if LLMs can now get the specific examples we published (and which are now presumably in the training set).
statement.document_title: Hard-forked! Casey Newton’s distorted portrait of Gary Marcus and AI skepticism

from_speaker: had trouble with causality, physical reasoning, psychological reasoning, mathematical reasoning
even if LLMs can now get the specific examples we published
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of December 2024, state-of-the-art LLMs still showed significant, documented failures in causal, physical, psychological (theory of mind) and mathematical reasoning on new or varied problems, beyond the 2020 examples.
'Psychological reasoning' is read as theory-of-mind and social reasoning.
Target period: the claim describes the state of LLMs when the post was written. I use 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-06, the most recent period public evaluations could report on before the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations published in 2024 show current LLMs failing or being fragile on held-out or perturbed tasks in each of the four areas.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evaluations from 2024 show frontier LLMs performing reliably at or near human level on new and perturbed tasks in these areas, so that 'trouble' no longer fairly describes them.

evidence.excerpt: Adding a single clause that seems relevant to the question causes significant performance drops (up to 65%) across all state-of-the-art models, even though the clause doesn't contribute to the reasoning chain needed for the final answer.
evidence.explanation: Shows state-of-the-art LLMs breaking on small changes to grade-school math problems. That is continued trouble with mathematical reasoning beyond memorized examples.

evidence.excerpt: state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) often rely on superficial heuristics -- for example, inferring causality from event order or recalling memorized world knowledge without attending to context.
evidence.explanation: Finds causal reasoning in current LLMs relies on shallow heuristics. That supports continued trouble with causality.

evidence.excerpt: Our results show that LLMs are currently outperformed by human children on these tasks.
evidence.explanation: On embodied physical common-sense tasks (tracking hidden objects, tool use), state-of-the-art multimodal LLMs did worse than children. That supports continued trouble with physical reasoning.

evidence.excerpt: The overall low goal accuracy across all evaluated models indicates only a limited degree of ToM capabilities.
evidence.explanation: Finds limited theory-of-mind ability on varied tasks. This supports trouble with psychological reasoning, though only open-source models were tested.

evidence.excerpt: o1 averaged 74% (11.1/15) with a single sample per problem, 83% (12.5/15) with consensus among 64 samples
evidence.explanation: Shows a large 2024 jump in competition-math performance. This cuts against how severe the math 'trouble' is, though it does not show robustness under perturbation.

evidence.excerpt: GPT-4 models performed at, or even sometimes above, human levels at identifying indirect requests, false beliefs and misdirection, but struggled with detecting faux pas.
evidence.explanation: A peer-reviewed study finding human-level GPT-4 performance on several theory-of-mind tests. This partly cuts against the psychological-reasoning part, though it also notes struggles with faux pas.
